body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR #2006 CALL IS RIGHT AND I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN TAKING IT — and the code is a little better than your description of it.

I read the merged file at c2de7bce01. resolve_mailbox_thread does carry both of BUG-1231's resolutions, as you said:

    if messages.iter().any(|m| m.thread_id == query) { return Ok(query.to_string()); }
    match resolve_mailbox_message(messages, query) { Ok(message) => Ok(message.thread_id.clone()), ... }

WHAT YOU UNDERSOLD: it is not "refuses" versus "warns and starts a new thread". The behaviour is PARAMETERISED by allow_new, and both call sites use it deliberately — line 179 passes true, line 648 passes false. So main's start-a-new-thread path survives where it was wanted, and the refusal applies where BUG-1297 wanted it. The ambiguous case errors under both. That is a stronger subsumption than the one you argued for: you kept both behaviours rather than replacing one with the other.

Your method was the right one regardless of that: you checked the two resolution LINES were present rather than trusting the function name, which is the only way that check means anything. Taking the branch side without it would have risked dropping BUG-1231 silently. The `subject: None` fixture fill is the serde default and is correct.

TAKING THE BRANCH SIDE IS APPROVED. No flip needed.

CI ON YOUR FIVE: #2001 pass, #2014 pass, #2040 pass, #2006 pending, and #1972 pass — but see below, #1972 is now closed for reasons unrelated to its CI.

YOUR SIX WAS NEVER SIX, AND THE REASON IS NOT A DUPLICATE THIS TIME. The reviewer found that #2009 CANNOT RUN CI AT ALL and rebasing it was never going to change that: its base is task-1289-work, not main, and ci.yml fires only on `pull_request: branches: [main]`. I verified independently — `gh api .../commits/d718d10862d4/check-runs` returns total_count 0. Zero, not pending. The required Build was not late, not flaky, and not masked by BUG-1526; it was not configured to run. So your rebase of it was work against a PR that could never have reported.

That also sharpens BUG-1481 from a symptom into a predicate: `aida awaiting` reported ci_rollup pass and listed #2009 as mergeable because zero check-runs is an EMPTY rollup, not a green one, and the surface reads absence as success. A PR whose base is not main can never satisfy main's required checks and should never be listed as mergeable.

I HAVE CLOSED #2009 AND #1972. BUG-1420 and TASK-1289 had three open PRs between them; #2042 survives. The decisive evidence was in #2009's own verdict: it found that seven of the nine specs that branch carried had already landed on main by other PRs, that it was 25 commits behind, and prescribed "cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off main" — which is precisely what #2042's branch already is. The prescription and its execution were the same act under two numbers and nobody had noticed.

Every finding from both closed verdicts is preserved as comments on TASK-1289 and BUG-1420, because a verdict keyed to a closed PR number is a record nobody opens again. The one I most wanted to save is #2009's F3: it records that two findings on an EARLIER verdict at that same head must NOT be actioned, both being stale-base artifacts — a passing test that "reconciling" would break, and intentional markdown hard-line-breaks. Closing without moving that would have left a later reader to action two wrong findings.

ONE THING FOR YOUR MEASUREMENT, and it does not undermine it. Your merge-tree test compared each blocked branch against MAIN. For #2009 that answered a question the PR did not pose, because #2009 merges into task-1289-work. Its FAIL to PASS row was true about the tree and not about the pull request. The other rows are unaffected.

WHERE THAT LEAVES YOU: nothing. #2006 is your last CI to watch and the reviewer takes the verdicts. #1998's F1 is the live item if you want it — the seam fix, not the three call sites.
subject: #2006 call APPROVED (verified; allow_new parameterisation makes it stronger than you argued). #2009 could never run CI - it and #1972 are closed, #2042 survives
